# Job Chapter 8 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 418v–419r

---

**1** Then Bildad from Shuah spoke up:

**2** "How long are you going to talk like this?
Your words are nothing but bluster!

**3** Does God twist justice?
Does the Almighty distort what is right?

**4** If your children sinned against him,
he gave them over to the consequences of their sin.

**5** But if you yourself will earnestly seek God
and plead with the Almighty,

**6** and if you are truly pure and upright,
then he will surely rise up on your behalf
and restore your prosperous home.

**7** Even if your beginnings were modest,
your future will be beyond anything you can imagine.

**8** Just ask the previous generation.
Pay attention to what their ancestors discovered.

**9** We are only here since yesterday and know so little —
our days on earth pass like a shadow.

**10** Won't they teach you? Won't they tell you?
Won't they share the wisdom they have gained?

**11** Can papyrus grow tall without a marsh?
Can reeds thrive without water?

**12** Even while they are still green and not yet cut,
they wither faster than any other plant.

**13** That is the fate of everyone who forgets God.
The hope of the godless comes to nothing.

**14** What they trust in is fragile;
what they rely on is a spider's web.

**15** They lean on their house, but it collapses;
they grab hold of it, but it gives way.

**16** The wicked are like a well-watered plant in the sunshine,
spreading its shoots over the whole garden.

**17** Its roots wrap around a pile of rocks;
it clings to a foundation of stone.

**18** But when it is torn from its spot,
the ground disowns it: 'I never knew you.'

**19** That is all the 'joy' it will ever know,
and from the same soil, other plants will take its place.

**20** The point is this: God does not reject an innocent person,
and he does not support evildoers.

**21** He will fill your mouth with laughter again
and your lips with shouts of joy.

**22** Your enemies will be covered in shame,
and the homes of the wicked will disappear."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**"He gave them over to their sin" (v.4):** This is the cruelest line any of the friends speak. Bildad casually suggests that Job's children deserved to die. He says it almost in passing, as a stepping stone to his main point about Job's own prospects. The reader, who watched ten young people crushed by a wind sent at the Adversary's instigation, knows how monstrously wrong this is.

**The appeal to tradition (vv.8-10):** Bildad's authority is ancestral wisdom. He freely admits that his own generation knows nothing ("we are but of yesterday"), but he believes the accumulated wisdom of the fathers is sufficient. Job's radical stance is that his own experience trumps inherited tradition — a profoundly modern claim embedded in an ancient text.

**"God does not reject an innocent person" (v.20):** Bildad's conclusion is logically airtight and experientially false. It is true as a general principle of divine justice, but it fails spectacularly when applied to Job. The entire book is a case study in the gap between theological principle and lived reality.

---
*— PNEUMA*
